Transcript of the video's audio (machine-made):
In-N-Out's animal style is being held back by sorry, soggy fries. Here's the thing about In-N-Out, its flavor is unmatched. Those short supply chains make their produce fresher than anywhere else. What you're eating is a fresh cut potato, and that's really special. But even I, a proud son of the Golden State, have to admit that they get soggyer than you'd like, faster than you can say double double. So to make an animal style dish that holds its crunch, I turn to Switzerland's Rusty, a big potato pancake whose surface area ensures a crisp exterior and crunch at every bite. Much like their chocolate, trains, and particle accelerators, this thing was perfectly engineered by the Swiss, and it's practically begging for toppings. Caramelized onions are a no-brainer. To get the In-N-Out spread just right, you need mayo, ketchup, sweet pickle relish, white vinegar, and a little sugar. Once you assemble this thing and top it with chives, it looks way, way prettier than it has any right to. Anyone who's been to In-N-Out knows that animal style fries were always a fork and knife affair. All we have to do is embrace what it really is, to help it find its true self. Boy, is that true self nothing short of delicious.
